next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Elections Current/Past

glance_notes.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Voter Information
glance_notes.text: No Voter Registration: North Dakota is the only state that does not require voter registration. Eligible residents do not register before voting. Instead, voters establish eligibility through North Dakota's voter qualification and identification requirements.

glance_notes.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Voter ID Requirements
glance_notes.text: Voter ID Required: North Dakota requires voters to provide qualifying identification when voting. Standard forms include a North Dakota driver's license, North Dakota nondriver identification card, qualifying tribal identification or tribal documentation, and a long-term care certificate. Supplemental documentation may be used when required information on an otherwise valid ID is missing or outdated.

glance_notes.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Absentee Voting: Any qualified North Dakota elector may request an absentee ballot without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, domestic absentee ballots become available September 24. Applications must be submitted by November 2, and completed ballots must be received by the appropriate election official by the close of polls on Election Day.

register.label: Voter Eligibility — No Registration Required
register.content: North Dakota does not have voter registration. An eligible resident does not submit a voter registration application before voting. To qualify as a North Dakota elector, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old on Election Day, be a North Dakota resident and have resided in the applicable precinct for at least 30 days immediately before the election. The voter must also be able to establish eligibility using the identification procedures required by North Dakota law.
register.glance_value: No voter registration in North Dakota
register.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Voter Information
register.internal_note: North Dakota is unique among the states because it has no voter-registration requirement. Do not provide a registration deadline or registration application. NDCC 16.1-01-04 establishes the elector qualifications, including citizenship, age, state residency and 30-day precinct residency. North Dakota maintains a Central Voter File for election administration and voter verification, but this is not a voter-registration system.

check_registration.label: Check Voting Information
check_registration.content: Because North Dakota does not have voter registration, there is no registration status to check. Instead, use the state's My Voting Information portal to find voting information for your address, including polling locations and sample-ballot information. Voters should also make sure the residential address associated with their qualifying identification is current or be prepared to provide acceptable supplemental documentation.
check_registration.glance_value: No registration to check; use My Voting Information
check_registration.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — My Voting Information
check_registration.internal_note: The My Voting Information portal allows searches using state-issued ID information or residential address. The Secretary of State also provides an NDDOT address-update link because current residential-address information is important to North Dakota's voter-ID system.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: North Dakota has no voter registration and therefore has no voter registration deadline. A person who meets North Dakota's elector qualifications, including the 30-day residency requirement, may vote if the person satisfies the state's identification and voting requirements. Voters should update their identification address or gather qualifying supplemental documentation before voting to avoid delays.
deadlines.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Voter Information
deadlines.internal_note: Do not invent a registration deadline for North Dakota. There is none. The relevant timing requirement is that an elector generally must have resided in the precinct for at least 30 days immediately before the election. Absentee voting has separate application and ballot-return deadlines.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use North Dakota's My Voting Information portal to find Election Day polling locations and voting information specific to your address. North Dakota counties use different election-administration models, including traditional precinct polling sites and vote centers. Every North Dakota county has at least one polling location open on Election Day. Voters should check the official portal shortly before voting because locations and hours are determined locally and can vary.
polling_place.glance_value: Use My Voting Information for local polling locations
polling_place.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — My Voting Information
polling_place.internal_note: North Dakota's current election system includes traditional precinct sites, vote centers and vote-by-mail counties. However, the Secretary of State explicitly confirms that all counties have Election Day polling locations. Avoid describing vote-by-mail counties as having no in-person Election Day voting. The statewide polling-place database should be rechecked after 2026 General Election locations and hours are finalized.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: North Dakota's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Election Day polling hours are established locally within limits set by state law. Polls must open no later than 9:00 a.m. and may open as early as 7:00 a.m. Polls must remain open until at least 7:00 p.m. and may remain open as late as 9:00 p.m. Anyone standing in line when the polling location's designated closing time arrives must be allowed to vote. Voters must satisfy North Dakota's identification requirements.
election_day.glance_value: Hours vary locally; generally within 7:00 a.m. – 9:00 p.m.
election_day.internal_note: North Dakota does NOT have one uniform statewide opening and closing time. NDCC 16.1-01-03 requires polls to open at 9:00 a.m. or earlier, but not earlier than 7:00 a.m., and close at 7:00 p.m. or later, but not later than 9:00 p.m., as designated locally. Local polling-hour determinations must be made and reported to the county auditor no later than 30 days before the election. This section should therefore be reverified once the November 2026 statewide polling-place list is finalized.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: North Dakota does not use one uniform Election Day schedule statewide. Each precinct's hours are established locally within state-law limits. Polls must open between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. and must close between 7:00 p.m. and 9:00 p.m. Voters who are standing in line at the designated closing time must be allowed to vote. Check My Voting Information for the exact hours at your voting location.
polling_hours.glance_value: Local hours within 7:00 a.m. – 9:00 p.m. limits
polling_hours.internal_note: This is an important North Dakota distinction. State law permits different precinct schedules. Do not simplify this to a statewide 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. or 9:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. schedule. Governing bodies establish hours within the statutory range, and voters already in line at closing are protected.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: North Dakota permits counties and communities to offer in-person early voting, but early voting is not provided under one uniform statewide schedule and is not available in every county. Participating counties establish their own early-voting locations, dates and hours. Voters should use the state's My Voting Information and statewide polling-location resources to determine whether early voting is offered in their county for the November 3, 2026 General Election and, if so, where and when.
early_voting.glance_value: Available in some counties; dates and hours vary
early_voting.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — How Do I Vote
early_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State explicitly states that some communities offer early voting. The statewide election database identifies which counties offer it and publishes locations and hours. General Election early-voting schedules were not sufficiently finalized statewide as of August 30, so do not invent a statewide October date range. Reverify after counties publish November schedules.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Vote-by-Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any qualified North Dakota elector may request an absentee ballot without providing an excuse. Voters are not automatically mailed a ballot without first requesting one. In vote-by-mail counties, voting-age residents are mailed an absentee-ballot application and may decide whether to request the ballot or vote in person. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, domestic absentee ballots become available September 24 and the absentee application submission deadline is November 2. Completed absentee ballots must be received by the appropriate election official by the close of polls on Election Day. Ballots may be returned by mail, to an authorized county drop box or directly to the county auditor, but they cannot be returned to an Election Day polling location.
absentee_mail.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: This reflects a significant current rule: North Dakota's Secretary of State now states that absentee ballots must be RECEIVED by close of polls on Election Day. Older materials that describe a day-before-Election-Day postmark deadline should not be relied upon for the 2026 General Election. The official 2026 current-election page lists September 24 as the beginning of domestic absentee voting, November 2 as the application deadline and November 3 as the ballot receipt deadline. All counties have Election Day polling locations even where vote-by-mail is used.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: North Dakota requires qualifying identification to vote. Standard acceptable forms include a valid North Dakota driver's license, North Dakota nondriver identification card, tribal-government identification or qualifying tribal documentation, and a long-term care certificate issued by a North Dakota facility. Identification used for ordinary in-person voting must establish the voter's legal name, current residential address and date of birth. If otherwise valid identification does not contain all required information or contains outdated information, the voter may provide qualifying supplemental documentation. A voter who cannot establish eligibility at the polling place may cast a set-aside ballot and provide qualifying identification or documentation before the county canvassing board meets.
voter_id.glance_value: ID required; supplemental documentation and set-aside ballot available
voter_id.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.internal_note: NDCC 16.1-01-04.1 and the 2026 Election Officials Manual establish the identification requirement. A voter lacking sufficient ID at the polls does not simply lose the ability to vote; a set-aside ballot procedure is available, with documentation provided before the canvassing board meeting. Tribal voters have additional address-documentation options. Absentee and UOCAVA voters have some different identification procedures, including an attester option in qualifying absentee circumstances.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: North Dakota provides assistance and accessible voting equipment for voters who need accommodations. The ExpressVote assistive ballot-marking device is available as part of the state's voting system and may be used by any voter. Voters who need assistance at a polling location may receive accommodations without being required to disclose the nature of a disability. North Dakota also provides special identification procedures in certain circumstances, including long-term care certificates and an attester option for qualifying absentee voters who are unable to obtain identification because of a disability.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Assistive voting equipment and accommodations available
accessible_voting.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Voting Equipment
accessible_voting.internal_note: The 2026 Election Officials Manual includes detailed guidance for assisting voters with disabilities and states that voters are not required to disclose why they need accommodation or assistance. The Secretary of State confirms that ExpressVote assistive ballot-marking devices are part of North Dakota's voting equipment. The absentee application system expressly provides an attester option for voters unable to obtain ID because of disability.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: North Dakota provides special absentee-voting procedures for eligible members of the Uniformed Services, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application and federal voting-assistance procedures. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, UOCAVA ballots are made available beginning September 18. A military ID may be used when applying for a UOCAVA ballot by an eligible military voter stationed away from the voter's North Dakota residence, and a U.S. passport may be used in qualifying overseas circumstances. Voters who instead vote in person in North Dakota must meet the state's ordinary in-person identification requirements.
military_overseas.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Military and Overseas U.S. Citizens
military_overseas.internal_note: The official 2026 Election & Candidate Filing Guide establishes September 18, 2026, the 46th day before the General Election, as the UOCAVA ballot-availability date. The Secretary of State's current UOCAVA page distinguishes identification accepted for remote UOCAVA applications from identification required when voting in person in North Dakota. Do not tell an in-person voter that a military ID or passport alone satisfies ordinary North Dakota polling-place ID requirements.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student may vote in North Dakota if the student meets the state's elector qualifications, including North Dakota residency and at least 30 days of residence in the applicable precinct before Election Day. A North Dakota student attending school away from the student's permanent North Dakota residence may continue voting from that home residence if it remains the student's voting residence, including by absentee ballot. A student who establishes residence in the college community may vote there after meeting the residency requirement and updating identification or providing the qualifying student documentation permitted by state law. A student who remains a resident of another state should vote under that state's rules rather than voting in North Dakota.
student_voting.glance_value: Vote from one qualifying North Dakota residence
student_voting.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — College Students Voting
student_voting.internal_note: North Dakota specifically allows a student whose valid North Dakota ID shows a different North Dakota address from the student's current residence to supplement that ID with qualifying documentation issued by the institution of higher education, including required identifying information, together with a student photo ID. The older student handout contains an outdated absentee postmark statement, so it is relied upon here only for student-residency concepts that remain consistent with current law and current ID guidance. Current absentee return deadlines come from the 2026 Secretary of State guidance instead.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: North Dakota voters can use the state's My Voting Information portal to view a sample ballot for the upcoming election based on their voting address. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's precinct and local contests, voters should use their own address information to retrieve the applicable ballot. County auditors are also required to publish election notices and sample ballots before the General Election.
sample_ballot.glance_value: View your sample ballot in My Voting Information
sample_ballot.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — My Voting Information
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary of State's Elections page directly states that My Voting Information can be used to find a polling place and view a sample ballot. The official 2026 Election & Candidate Filing Guide states that county auditors must publish a notice of election and sample ballot once a week for two consecutive weeks before the General Election under NDCC 16.1-11-21. Reverify voter-specific November ballots after final ballot preparation.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: North Dakota Secretary of State, Elections Division, 600 East Boulevard Avenue, Department 108, Bismarck, ND 58505-0500. Phone: 701-328-4146. Toll-free: 800-352-0867, extension 328-4146. Email: soselect@nd.gov. County auditors administer many local election functions and should be contacted for questions about specific polling locations, early voting, absentee ballots and county voting procedures.
contact.source_name: North Dakota Secretary of State — Elections Division
contact.internal_note: Current Secretary of State election materials verify 600 East Boulevard Avenue, Department 108, Bismarck, ND 58505-0500; 701-328-4146; 800-352-0867 extension 328-4146; and [soselect@nd.gov](mailto:soselect@nd.gov). The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the North Dakota Secretary of State Elections website and My Voting Information portal for official statewide voter information. These resources provide voter qualification and identification guidance, polling locations, sample ballots, absentee-ballot applications, ballot tracking and election information. County auditors administer polling locations, early voting, absentee voting and other local election functions.
